_about: Architecture facts for the released models the demo carries beside the OV50 arms, from the papers and the released code, cited per model. No measured number is typed here: parameter counts come from the checkpoints (sota/count_params.py -> sota/params.json, which sums the state-dict tensors under each block's `count` prefixes; `count_whole` = every tensor of the loaded dict falls in some block), RTFs from sota/run_models.py's _run.json, and every evaluation number from sota/work/*/score_*.json via demo/tools/make_results_sota.py. Figures left in the prose are configuration (FFT sizes, step counts, rates), not results. `seen_basis` says whether the training-set list is the paper's split (`stated`) or an assumption (`assumed`).

flowhigh.name: FLowHigh
flowhigh.paper: Yun, Kim, Lee. FLowHigh: Towards Efficient and High-Quality Audio Super-Resolution with Single-Step Flow Matching. ICASSP 2025. arXiv:2501.04926
flowhigh.family: flow matching, mel domain, one Euler step, neural vocoder
flowhigh.params_note: the flow model and the BigVGAN vocoder, both in the released checkpoint and both run at inference
flowhigh.det_note: Stochastic by design, deterministic as shipped: inference.py passes std_2 without std_1, so sample() resets the noise scale to σ and every draw is the same to within rounding. Restoring the trained prior does not bring the spread back: one Euler step from t = 0 returns the conditional mean for any noise.
flowhigh.input: resample_poly to 48 kHz, peak-normalised; mel spectrogram 2048/480, 256 mels, 0–24 kHz

blocks.label: mel front end
blocks.detail: STFT 2048 / hop 480 / 256 mel bands at 48 kHz

blocks.label: flow transformer
blocks.detail: 2 layers, 16 heads × 64, independent CFM (adaptive), σ = 1e-4; x₀ = the input's mel + noise → x₁ = the target's mel in ONE Euler step

blocks.label: post-processing
blocks.detail: STFT-domain low-band replacement from the input below the 99 %-cumulative-energy bin; output peak-normalised to 0.99

flowhigh.training: VCTK 0.92, the NU-Wave 2 split (100 speakers train; p360–p376, s5 test), 400 k steps
flowhigh.seen_note: p236–p238 are in its training set; p360, p361, p374 are not
flowhigh.context: a whole mel frame (2048 samples = 43 ms) and, through attention, the whole utterance

apbwe.name: AP-BWE
apbwe.paper: Lu, Ai, Du, Ling. Towards High-Quality and Efficient Speech Bandwidth Extension with Parallel Amplitude and Phase Prediction. IEEE/ACM TASLP 2024. arXiv:2401.06387
apbwe.family: amplitude + phase spectrum prediction, GAN-trained, deterministic
apbwe.params_note: generator only; the discriminators are training-time
apbwe.det_note: A point estimate: one output per input.
apbwe.input: torchaudio (sinc) resample to 48 kHz; STFT 1024 / hop 80 / win 320; log-amplitude and phase spectra. Not level-invariant: fed at the corpus's stored level, since a peak-normalised input scores worse

blocks.label: STFT
blocks.detail: 1024 / 80 / 320 at 48 kHz → log-amplitude and phase, 513 bins

blocks.label: amplitude stream
blocks.detail: 8 ConvNeXt blocks, 512 channels, with cross-connections to the phase stream

blocks.label: phase stream
blocks.detail: 8 ConvNeXt blocks, 512 channels; phase parallel-estimated (two-component + anti-wrapping)

apbwe.training: VCTK 0.92 train split (test = p360–p376, s5); GAN losses (multi-period + multi-resolution discriminators) + amplitude, phase and STFT losses
apbwe.seen_note: p236–p238 are in its training set; p360, p361, p374 are not
apbwe.context: the whole spectrum of a 6.7 ms frame; ConvNeXt kernels spanning tens of frames

nuwave2.name: NU-Wave 2
nuwave2.paper: Han, Lee. NU-Wave 2: A General Neural Audio Upsampling Model for Various Sampling Rates. Interspeech 2022. arXiv:2206.08545
nuwave2.params_note: every weight of the network, counted from the checkpoint
nuwave2.det_note: A sampler: eight DDIM steps from Gaussian noise; each seed is a different draw.
nuwave2.input: Chebyshev-8 low-pass (0.05 dB) + resample_poly down and back up to 48 kHz; the band mask (input Nyquist) conditions every layer

blocks.label: Gaussian noise
blocks.detail: z ~ N(0, I) at 48 kHz, the same length as the input

blocks.label: noise-level embedding
blocks.detail: log-SNR embedding, and the input, skip and output projections

blocks.label: 15 residual layers
blocks.detail: 64 channels; each with a short-time Fourier convolution (STFC: STFT → conv on real/imag → iSTFT) and a bandwidth spectral feature transform (BSFT) conditioned on the band mask

blocks.label: 8 DDIM steps
blocks.detail: fixed log-SNR schedule (−2.6 … 17.2); the input waveform is concatenated at every step

nuwave2.training: VCTK 0.92, 100 train speakers (p360–p376, s5 held out); input rates drawn uniformly 6–48 kHz with random Chebyshev filters
nuwave2.seen_note: p236–p238 are in its training set; p360, p361, p374 are not
nuwave2.context: STFC frames of 1024 samples (21 ms); the residual stack sees the whole clip

audiosr.name: AudioSR (speech)
audiosr.paper: Liu, Chen, Tian, Wang, Plumbley. AudioSR: Versatile Audio Super-Resolution at Scale. ICASSP 2024. arXiv:2309.07314
audiosr.family: latent diffusion on a mel VAE, 50 DDIM steps, HiFi-GAN vocoder
audiosr.params_note: the diffusion U-Net, the conditioning VAE's encoder and the VAE decoder with its vocoder, all run at inference; the EMA copy, the CLAP model and the first-stage encoder in the checkpoint are not
audiosr.det_note: A sampler: 50 DDIM steps with classifier-free guidance; each seed is a different draw. Its low band also varies from draw to draw, so its full-band spread is wider than its high-band spread.
audiosr.input: resampled to 48 kHz and padded to a multiple of 5.12 s; the cutoff is located from the input's own spectrum (98.5 % cumulative energy) and a random low-pass of that cutoff makes the conditioning mel

blocks.label: mel + VAE encoder
blocks.detail: 48 kHz mel (2048/480, 256 bands) → latent, 12.8 latent frames per second

blocks.label: latent diffusion U-Net
blocks.detail: conditioned on the low-passed mel; 50 DDIM steps, guidance scale 3.5

blocks.label: post-processing
blocks.detail: the input's low band replaces the output's below the located cutoff

audiosr.training: a large multi-domain set (speech, music, sound effects) that includes VCTK; the speech checkpoint is fine-tuned on speech
audiosr.seen_note: VCTK is in its training data and the paper does not state a speaker split; assume every VCTK speaker was seen
audiosr.context: 5.12 s windows through a U-Net with attention: the whole window
